This framework has the potential to simplify studies of hypergraph operations and enable classification of new hypergraph types based on their building blocks.

India's next-generation space observatory, the INSIST, will significantly contribute to the study of the universe by focusing on the analysis of distant galaxies and young stars near the Earth. To achieve this, it will be equipped with advanced imaging capabilities and two high-resolution spectrograph instruments that can detect and analyze the chemical composition of cosmic objects at specific wavelengths. By utilizing data-driven observations, INSIST will capture images of the Earth in the infrared spectrum, thereby providing valuable insights into the chemical evolution of the universe and facilitating the detection of exoplanets.

In clinical trials, the mixed model repeated measures is commonly used for comparing continuous outcomes over time. However, typically only categorical time is used in MMRM, which implicitly assumes a linear trend in the data. We provide evidence that this assumption may not hold, especially when there are missing at random data, potentially resulting in biased estimates. We explored the feasibility of utilizing continuous time as a numerical variable in MMRM, along with its limitations and applications.

The principle of the Onsager-Machlup action is used to assess how likely a reaction pathway is for a given system, allowing us to identify its most probable route. This concept has been applied to identify equilibrium paths in materials such as silicon dioxide. Our study involved analyzing the equilibrium paths for growing silicon dioxide layers on silicon substrates by examining the growth front's progression into the substrate. We identified three distinct growth mechanisms for different substrate orientations, which align with the known "linear-linear-parabolic" growth behavior. By comparing our findings to traditional transition state theory and molecular simulations, we found some discrepancies but also observed good agreement under molten oxide equilibrium conditions. This technique offers valuable insights into reaction pathways in chemical engineering, particularly in solidification and dissolution processes.

This study focuses on a parabolic variant of complex Monge-Ampere equations and utilizes a PDE-based method akin to Phong et al to derive and establish L-infinity and Holder estimates. Moreover, the research expands upon these L-infinity estimates to encompass a broader category of parabolic Hessian equations.

Building on the tree automata model of Courcelles and Moser, we develop a framework for computing on trees in automated and efficient ways. Polyregular functions, which comprise the closure under composition of several classes of tree functions, exhibit specific growth rates. We demonstrate that these growth rates can be characterized as asymptotic solutions to homogeneous systems of asymptotic equations derived from the tree automata model. Furthermore, we automatically determine the exact growth rate of any polyregular function by exploiting properties of the matrix representation of its corresponding tree automaton.

This concise note establishes a relationship between Ito and Stratonovich integrals when conditional measure flow components are involved in the integrands, with the 'correction' term requiring consideration of the typical sample path behavior. As the typical path behavior of conditional measure flows differs from standard time-based measures, this "correction" term cannot be disregarded in relevant applications. Conditional measure flows play a crucial role in constructing solutions to stochastic differential equations through piecewise multiple stochastic integrals and are increasingly utilized in the analysis of conditional mean-field games.

This research aims to investigate various types of primitive subgroups within
the framework of normal subgroups. Different primitive configurations have
been proposed, including andesitic, herps, herp-subgroups and primitive
normal subgroups. The paper will present a comprehensive approach using
category theory, focusing on herp-subgroups as generators in an
interchangeability system. Through this method, we define primitive herp-
subgroups as generators of the free herp-category and establish their
relationship with the free herp-subgroups. The paper concludes by examining
the inherent herp-subgroups of a monoid and demonstrating their universal
applicability.

This study addresses the challenge of generating high-quality SQL queries from natural language text within a single model framework. It focuses on key components of the task: establishing a strong link between natural language and SQL, and effectively leveraging cross-database information. To tackle the first aspect, we propose a novel attention-based model called Attentional Neural U2S (ANU2U), which incorporates a universal SQL representation to improve the task's scalability. For the second aspect, we introduce a novel data enhancement technique, which leverages the full potential of schema information to boost the model's robustness. Our comprehensive evaluations on the SchemaGLUE dataset have yielded superior performance, specifically an increase of 3.1% in the F1-score compared to existing methods. The proposed methods and findings are available at https://github.com/ashwini111111/SchemaGLUE-Solution.

In complex multi-robot systems, accurately navigating while avoiding potential collisions poses a significant challenge due to the presence of uncertainty in robot positioning. To address this, we develop an advanced point-cloud map representation and propose an innovative depth-based obstacle avoidance method within this framework. By leveraging a deep learning approach, we effectively estimate a set of possible robot trajectories based on real-world robot observations and uncertainty estimates. This method allows us to calculate a robust conditional value-at-risk metric for estimating collision probabilities, and we specifically apply it to a depth-based obstacle avoidance strategy called depth-OAR, which further facilitates the development of a fast and reliable multi-robot system. Our approach demonstrates notable advantages in terms of reduced computation time and collision rates compared to existing methods through a comparison with the state-of-the-art.

Recent discoveries of ultra-faint dwarf (UFD) galaxies around the Milky Way have led to a reevaluation of their role in understanding dark matter and its interactions. A key area of interest is whether these galaxies host ancient stellar populations or have been influenced by external events. Our research focuses on a new metal-poor globular cluster, Andromeda XXV, which is located in a dwarf spheroidal galaxy orbiting the Andromeda galaxy. We have identified two other similar, yet unassociated, globular clusters in the Andromeda galaxy's vicinity with extremely low metallicities and metal-poor spectra. Our analysis of their spectra and other data, such as their positions and velocities, reveals a previously unknown, extremely metal-poor stellar stream, which is part of a larger, larger-scale structure, and is a result of the ongoing interaction between the Andromeda galaxy and the Milky Way. Our findings also reveal a new, extremely metal-poor stellar population in a dwarf spheroidal galaxy in the Andromeda galaxy's halo. Our research focuses on a new, extremely metal-poor globular cluster, Andromeda XXV, which is located in a dwarf spheroidal galaxy in the Milky Way's neighborhood, and is part of a larger, larger-scale structure, which is part of the Milky Way's neighboring galaxy, the Andromeda galaxy. Our research reveals a new, extremely metal-poor stellar population in the Andromeda galaxy's halo. Our research

In massive machine-type communications (mMTC), granting numerous user equipments (UEs) to access the network efficiently is crucial for future Internet of everything (IoEs) development. Traditional grant-based solutions are ineffective in this regard due to their reliance on extensive signaling required for uplink resource allocation. As a result, emerging technologies are being designed to support multiple UEs for uplink resource sharing without the need for scheduling grants, including grant-free access methods. These methods typically utilize repeat transmissions or reduce packet overhead to enhance reliability in mMTC. 

This paper provides a comprehensive comparison of repeat-based and shortened packet-based grant-free access techniques in terms of their performance, reliability, and latency. A key contribution of this study is the development of analytical models that assess these metrics for various repeat and shortening-based grant-free patterns. The performance comparison of these patterns reveals that combining the use of repeat and shortening strategies can significantly improve reliability while minimizing retransmission overhead in uplink resource scheduling for mMTC.

A mathematical framework for moist air thermodynamics is developed using a combination of the fundamental energy equation and the alternative thermodynamic potential concepts, specifically the Helmholtz, Gibbs, and Enthalpy potentials. Each unique formulation is rigorously demonstrated to maintain thermodynamic equilibrium and consistency within a multi-phase, multi-component air system. A novel approach to include the heat of crystallization is introduced, presenting two distinct possibilities: an energy redistribution over the bulk system or heat release proportional to the change in water content. We establish the conditions under which these potential approaches yield equivalent thermodynamic outcomes and introduce a novel multi-scale model for snow particle growth. This model integrates the concepts of saturation adjustment and various growth rates for snow particles, where energy is either conserved or mixed entropy and redistributed, and growth heat energy is distributed over a scale. We examine the reliability of our model's approximation under various conditions and provide numerical validation of its performance in different atmospheric environments using Python simulations.

We introduce algebraic objects, which generalise ordered semirings and monoids, and extend these to objects that include elements acting as negative identities. An exterior algebra underlies this concept and it naturally incorporates Valuation Theory and Valued Fields into its framework. Furthermore, the monoids and semirings within exterior algebra exhibit relationships with Valuation Fields and Rationals, respectively, and the exterior algebra itself is part of a broader concept, which includes objects with multiple valuations instead of a single valuation.

This study introduces a novel spoken dialogue system representation, referred to as hypotheses confusion networks (CNs), which builds on existing top N ASR hypotheses. CNs allow for multiple best ASR hypotheses to be expressed within a single hypothesis, offering significant data efficiency advantages over conventional spoken dialogue systems. Furthermore, by representing hypotheses as graph-structured units, the proposed CN representation facilitates the CN-based maximum a posteriori decoding method's tractability. To validate the efficacy of the proposed representation and decoding strategy, CNs are derived from existing models and compared against baseline systems in the ARCTIC dataset's continuous speech evaluation task. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed CN representation achieves superior performance over baseline systems across multiple system components, including neural list-wise language models, beam search, and speech smoothing components.

We introduce new ways of quantifying semistable coherent sheaves on complex projective curves with a specific dimension these sheaves must have. Then, we apply the concepts of weighted finiteness and a modification of stable L-infinity categories to relate these quantifications. Subsequently, we use mathematical tools called Lefschetz-type formulas based on the work of Feynman-Manin categories, which we referred to as the sheaf category, to compute these quantifications. Finally, our calculations yield formulae for sheaves that exist on low-genus curves, curves low-degree in the complex projective line, and rational curves of any degree.

A critical factor in secret sharing schemes is the count of minimal qualified subsets, as this number directly impacts both efficiency and feasibility in terms of size. Specifically, a key open question revolves around whether it's possible to achieve exponential efficiency in universal access structures. This structure, a notable variant, relies on probabilistic schemes that, despite being efficient in achieving subset entropy minimization, have so far failed to confirm or deny the existence of a universal, exponentially efficient structure. Researchers have now resolved this query in the affirmative, finding a universal access structure that achieves exponential efficiency by converting every access structure into an equivalent probabilistic scheme, thereby establishing a universal structure that efficiently shares any secret. This result not only achieves long-standing open questions in secret sharing schemes but also lays the groundwork for further exploration and has implications in other domains, including coding theory and network design.

Our investigation examines the attainable precision limits achievable through quantum correlations when estimating unknown parameters. To illustrate, we examine the role of entanglement in polarization qubits and its impact on precision, specifically in the context of two scenarios - the case of $N$ qubits using noisy channels, a task relevant to quantum imaging, and the more complex scenario of $M$ qubits employing interferometry to measure relative phases. Calculations reveal that employing entanglement generated via noisy channels may not necessarily yield the most optimal precision in all scenarios, while in interferometry setups, the use of entangled states often surpasses the use of mixed states or incoherent phase encoding, although some nuanced exceptions exist. Ultimately, we also utilize optimal measurement techniques to assess the full precision potential of these approaches.

The study of magnetic field formation in the turbulent plasma flow under magnetic field-free conditions is an essential aspect of modern plasma research.  "Petafields" are localized structures characterized by extremely localized, high-intensity magnetic fields, found in the pellet-edge structure of plasma turbulence, which carries parallel currents.  A comprehensive analysis is provided of the conditions necessary for the emergence of petafields in the pellet-driven turbulence, along with an assessment of their potential applications and the possibility of observation.  Pellet injection into a magnetic cage creates an enormous heat release, resulting in an intense heat release, massive pellet-driven plasma turbulence, and an unusual phenomenon where the mean magnetic field is anti-aligned with the plasma current.  Pellet-induced and strong plasma current-driven turbulence are found to possess comparable energy spectra, and pellet-driven turbulence generates localized, high-intensity magnetic field structures known as petafields.  The petafield strength is estimated to be on the order of a few tens of Gauss.  Petafields are believed to emerge in several areas of the pellet-driven turbulence, including the pellet-head and pellet-tail structures, and may have potential applications for the measurement of pellet dynamics and turbulence characteristics.  The pellet-driven petafields are predicted to be observable through the use of high-resolution magnetometers such as polarization-sensitive reflectometry and Doppler backscattering.

Recent studies have applied deep metric learning for continuous learning 
in a zero-forgetting manner.  A common challenge arises when limiting 
access to pre-trained models.  A novel approach called LiFi, where 
each task's parameters remain frozen after learning while ensuring 
classification of old images, is proposed to overcome this issue.  A 
metric learning method based on the LoG loss is utilized to initiate 
each task.  A selective sampling strategy enables the utilization of 
metrics from previous tasks for regularizing new ones.  A distinct 
advantage of LiFi is that when the model's capacity allows, it can 
incorporate multiple sampling strategies for better performance.  As 
expected, LiFis performance surpasses that of existing methods when 
access to the model is restricted.

As social media platforms grow, so does the prevalence of hate speech, which can lead to severe consequences such as depression, violence, and even suicide. While numerous research projects and campaigns have been initiated to combat this issue, accessible datasets representing diverse hate speech online remain scarce. Our study aims to contribute to the development of hate speech detection models by providing a comprehensive hate speech dataset grounded in Indian online context. This dataset is unique in its representation of varying levels of offensiveness in text, making it suitable for applications such as generating warnings and suggestions. Our analysis highlights the significance of contextual features in hate speech detection and demonstrates the effectiveness of deep learning models in this domain.

We explore the behavior of large networks of identical neurons, using the combination of continuous time mean field analysis and discrete time approximation. The approach allows us to apply the method of stochastic bifurcation analysis to understand how random fluctuations affect the outcomes of stable and unstable periodic solutions. Initially, we apply this technique to a ring network of neurons, showing how increasing noise can end endogenous stochastic bifurcations that transition the network from in-phase to out-of-phase dynamics. Next, we apply the same method to networks with varying in-degree distributions, finding that adding more connections to individual nodes can either enhance or dampen network oscillations. The findings indicate that during stochastic bifurcations, past network patterns may still have a lasting impact on the network dynamics.

Recent years have seen increasing interest in Automatic Program Repair (APR) with
numerous approaches being explored. One of the most promising directions is
generative adversarial networks (GANs), which have shown potential in
applied settings, but their use in APR remains relatively unexplored. 
This research aims to bridge this gap by introducing two novel GAN-based
applied APRs, which can generate diverse and high-quality repaired 
programs. Initial experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of these
applied repaired programs, supporting the feasibility of using GANs 
in APR.

This study introduces novel spectral inf-mutual information rate definitions for channels with and without memory. We focus on a class of channels defined by their capacity formulas, including memoryless and finite-state Markov channels. We establish a capacity region formula for interference channels composed of these generic components in terms of spectral inf-mutual information rates. For specific instances, like scalar band-limited AWARC, we develop a spectral inf-mutual information formula that relies on solving a system of linear equations involving the channel transition matrices.

The influence of a nuclear equation-of-state (EoS) was assessed by modifying various parts of a hydrodynamic model. It's been found that using parts of the model separately reveals clearer distinctions in model outcomes, whereas nuclear EoS has the most significant impact on flow coefficients, particularly by affecting the density of particles. To simulate 10-90% reaction planes better, a variable spatial slope was introduced and demonstrated improved results. Additionally, a fixed boundary condition was introduced that yielded similar results to using varying slopes. Furthermore, introducing variable diffusion parameters based on local conditions and reaction planes yielded better outcomes than employing a constant diffusion coefficient.

The rapid spread of the COVID-19 pandemic has overwhelmed healthcare systems worldwide, with early diagnosis being crucial for effective case management and to mitigate the burden on medical services. While existing methods primarily rely on clinical assessments, they prove challenging for large-scale screening. On the other hand, the worldwide surge in digital health services presents an opportunity to leverage data from routine health assessments and electronic health records to enhance case identification and spread prediction capabilities. Building upon this foundation, building-block models have proven successful in predicting disease outcomes and predicting patient recovery timelines. Our research expands on this approach by integrating data from multiple domains associated with the COVID-19 disease, including demographic, clinical, and screening data, in an effort to forecast the global trajectory of the virus, forecast risks at the country level, and allocate resources proactively. By employing an advanced multi-domain prediction framework, we aim to provide a more accurate representation of the COVID-19 trajectory, enabling governments to take strategic action and reduce the impact of the virus.

A Graph Neural Network (GNN) is an effective neural network architecture that processes graph-like data, yet it faces challenges due to graph data's limited availability, particularly in the context of wireless communication systems. To address this, this study surveys and analyzes the application of graph neural networks in wireless communication systems. The rationale behind using GNNs in wireless systems, along with their fundamental components, is explained. The research then explores specific use cases where graph neural networks have been successfully applied in various wireless communication scenarios. The review highlights the limitations of current architectures and suggests potential future research directions.

The lowest human development status is linked to the highest mortality rates, particularly from homicides. By analyzing the geographic distribution of homicides, researchers can uncover their social drivers and identify key areas where targeted interventions can be most effective. This study analyzes the demographic and spatial patterns of homicide in Brazil, and discovers that the Black population has the highest homicide rates. Furthermore, south-eastern regions of the country exhibit the highest density of both Black individuals and both genders affected by the highest homicide rates. As a result, policy makers should prioritize Black populations in south-eastern regions in their crime prevention and public health initiatives.

We investigate stochastic gradient descent with decreasing step sizes in order to minimize a smooth function over a convex set. Initially providing error bounds for stationary points under specific conditions, we then demonstrate the efficacy of an adaptively weighted method that incorporates historical information. This leads to an accelerated convergence of stochastic gradient descent to the optimal value of a smooth function when it is also strongly-convex, with convergence rates of the big-O types: 1/(k^n + a_k) for any a_k tending to infinity as k increases. For a strong matrix convex function with unit norm gradient, we show that the method converges to a non-zero point in the Hessian's null space. Additionally, we build upon our findings to derive new results on stochastic Newton's method, yielding it the same convergence rates to the optimal value as stochastic gradient descent but with improved step sizes, specifically, a factor of sqrt(k+1) improvement.

Axion and Axion-Like Particles emerge from canonic chiral solutions termed as a QCED axion that mitigate the strong-CP issue. Recent theoretical advancements in understanding UV completion of axions have led to novel concepts such as axion gauge, axion photon, and axion power, in which the term "axion gauge" encompasses the concepts of St\"uckelberg gauge, marginal gauge, massive gauge, tachyon gauge. Similarly, novel ideas such as axion photon, axion power, and derivatively coupled axions have been developed within this theoretical framework. Distinguishing between these concepts is crucial for their experimental detection. In this paper, we explore the interplay between axion UV completion and low-energy phenomenology by systematically introducing generic low-energy effects associated with these concepts. In particular, derivatively coupled axions offer an effective tool for distinguishing axion gauge, axion photon, and axion power signatures. Our research highlights the unification of these concepts within this theoretical framework.

The occupation number over time is examined for a bosonic oscillator coupled to heat baths with fermionic and bosonic components. This oscillator, having one or two degrees of freedom, lacks equilibrium. Such a system serves as a means to establish dynamic memory. Specifically, we establish criteria for historical "fermion" and "boson" data. "Fermion" data is encoded in the past transition probabilities, while historical "boson" requires involvement of negative-frequency modes, which are characteristic of non-standard oscillators.

We introduce a groundbreaking dataset, DexGraspingNet, offering an extensive collection of 1.2 million simulated dexterous grasp examples, surpassing current datasets significantly in terms of 100 x 100 x 100 pixel point clouds at 0.01 meters resolution. Our dataset encompasses a diverse range of 10,000 real-world objects, facilitated by the PyBullet dexterous grasping engine, enabling efficient data generation and diverse grasping poses. Building upon our dataset, we propose GNN, a generalized grasping network model featuring a large memory bank that allows it to adapt to new grasping tasks quickly, reducing memory requirements while improving performance relative to state-of-the-art models.

A novel approach is suggested to create individual, frame-by-frame MRI images that are uniquely suited for capturing respiratory movements in cancer patients, rather than creating a generic set of images. Building upon the previously successful CAI net, this technique revolves around two critical tasks: creating a generic set of respiratory images (CCIEs) and a motion compensation transformation (MCT). To compensate for respiratory movements, MCT utilizes a segmentation-based method that corrects image deformations. However, this approach fails in MRI scans due to the difficulty of obtaining precise boundary information. Therefore, this research proposes a deep learning method to create MCTs directly from data. Additionally, to improve the quality of individual respiratory images, a collaborative strategy combining prior knowledge and self-knowledge is implemented to accurately compensate for respiratory movements in each frame. Experimental results demonstrate that this technique outperforms existing methods in creating individual respiratory images for patients with lung cancer.

We propose Enhanced Knowledge Distillation (EKD) model compression, a Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) based approach that combines low rank methods with knowledge distillation to improve performance. EKA (Enhanced Knowledge Distillation Adapter) integrates knowledge distillation into LoRA's training process, thereby avoiding complete retraining of pretrained models while effectively adapting them to specific tasks. By adding a small number of adaptable parameters (LoRA) and incorporating knowledge distillation, EKA achieves superior performance compared to both full training and adapter-based approaches, particularly in natural language processing (NLS) tasks.

Two submersion functions from the set of two-dimensional real numbers to the set of real numbers are defined, and their respective level set foliations are examined. The equivalence of these functions topologically is established if there exists a continuous function that preserves orientation and maps one foliation to another. This equivalence is denoted as $\sim$. The relationship of equivalence is shown to be transitive but not fully characterizing when given two functions with distinct critical values, and specifically functions with non-zero limits at infinity are considered. The implications of this equivalence in relation to the construction of closed extensions of these functions, and their ability to achieve topological stability, are explored.

Ecosystems with unique plant arrangements are found worldwide and often appear to have a purpose in grazing systems. Yet, understanding the precise mechanisms behind grazing intensity's impact on plant patterns in arid environments is unclear. This study investigates the connection between grazing, plant patterns, and resource competition using the Individual-Plant Model, by focusing on mesquite trees in the southwestern USA. The results show that plant arrangement doesn't mitigate the effects of grazing; instead, it delays its impact. Specifically, clustering allows the ecosystem to withstand heavy grazing before reaching equilibrium. This study reveals that the primary function of plant arrangements isn't to protect from grazing but to delay its full expression.

A widely used technique known as CountSketch allows for the approximation of frequent items in a data stream with a specified error rate and accuracy. Recently, an innovative decentralized CountSketch approach was developed for group identification in a data stream setting, where traditional techniques are ineffective. In this approach, multiple distributed processors collaborate to maintain and update a shared frequency estimate of group entities, even in the presence of an adversary attempting to disrupt their operation. A CountSketch-based group frequent item finder was implemented within this model, with specific bounds on false positives and utilizing O((k+k/f)*(log n + log f)*log f) processors and a communication cost of O(k*γ*+(k+ k/f)*γ**(log n + log f)*log f) communicated words, where k represents frequent group entities, f denotes the data stream size, n represents the number of data items in a group, γ is a communication cost parameter, and + denotes standard addition as well as ignoring lower-order terms.

Our python-based program, auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC), demonstrates enhanced computational performance and robust accuracy across diverse chemical systems and parameters. Compared to its C++ counterpart, our program yields similar or superior results while utilizing less computational resources. It achieves this by presenting strong performance when run on single or multiple CPUs and servers, along with effective scaling capabilities on large GPU networks. Furthermore, our program's capabilities are exemplified through numerous successful applications in multiple quantum chemistry contexts, including complex molecules, fractional occupation cases, properties calculation, conformational structures, and complex reactions.

High-frequency trading significantly alters traditional stock market behavior. To explore game-theoretic implications, we focus on a simple continuous double auction model where high-frequency trading strategies are considered. We establish a rigorous approach to analyzing limiting strategies, allowing us to demonstrate that as time approaches zero, the outcome remains stable under certain conditions, even when trading frequencies are extremely low. In this framework, high-frequency trading can effectively be seen as a discrete-time double auction with increasingly smaller time intervals. Using a two-player model, we investigate limiting strategies, highlighting the role of computational power and establishing the link between high-frequency and low-frequency trading. Our key finding reveals that in general, equilibrium strategies in discrete-time auctions do not necessarily correspond to actions taken in continuous-time settings. Finally, we identify specific scenarios within our framework where the equilibrium outcomes in both discrete and continuous time coincide, and characterize efficient outcomes resulting from rational, loss-less trading.

We examine a mechanism design problem for selling $k$ items to unit-demand buyers with private valuations for each item, who may be units or bundles. Our research focuses on designing bounded-influence mechanisms, specifically differential privacy mechanisms, that achieve truthful outcomes while minimizing loss in expected revenue under strict privacy constraints. In scenarios where items are identical and only bought one per buyer, we can trace the exact boundary of mechanisms capable of achieving optimal privacy-efficiency pairs. We also extend our findings to distinct items and develop mechanisms outperforming current benchmarks within a general framework, which includes differential privacy mechanisms with strictly lower ex-post revenue loss than prior constructions.

To facilitate abstractive summarization, we've introduced an enhanced objective function that integrates structured data, specifically, entity-to-entity relationships within articles, into the summary generation process. To leverage this information effectively, we've developed a guided attention mechanism which incorporates signals from chains of related entities to enhance attention within the context of each sentence. This approach enables the inclusion of more detailed information in the summary and improves overall coherence. Experiments have demonstrated that our method surpasses state-of-the-art results on the SQuAD v1.1 dataset for sentence expansion tasks and the WikiSum dataset for full-summarization tasks. Open-source implementation of our model is available for further use.

This research presents new sufficient conditions for differentiating a function with n real variables, where these conditions are grounded in the differentiability of a related function with n-1 variables and are less restrictive than traditional criteria.

Human vocal synchronization during social interactions provides valuable information about a person's cognitive behaviors, revealing characteristics such as age, gender, and mental health status. To enhance the current status of automatic speech detection technology, a novel approach combining 3D deep learning with data augmentation using time-frequency magnitudes and log-stochastic intensity is employed. This method effectively improves speech detection accuracy in complex backgrounds when applied to the 3D RMBN3D model. By training this model on excess data, a necessary 96% accuracy is achieved without requiring labels. Notably, only a tiny fraction of 2% of manually annotated data was needed to obtain such high performance levels.

A recent study applied a realizability technique to establish the meaning of a quantum lambda calculus, which results in a multitude of acceptable typing rules, all of equal standing. Building upon this concept, we present a significant subset of typing rules, which formulates a versatile quantum calculus, accompanied by a corresponding categorical interpretation. Specifically, we outline a semantics based on an adjunction between the categories of spaces with linearly combined values and the category of sets with distributed values.

Analytical calculations have been performed for two types of quasiparticle excitation energies per particle in systems of up to seven electrons, involving both the Laughlin wavefunction and those of composite fermions. Numerical data were then gathered by evaluating the overlap between the exact eigenstates of the non-interacting composite fermions ground state and quasiparticle states that are exact eigenstates of the interacting Hamiltonian. Results in the form of tables were provided, covering energy excitation per particle for systems with up to seven electrons and varying flux values. Additionally, graphs were produced to show the large-distance asymptotic behavior of the quasiparticle wavefunctions for different quantums, $n$, up to 5, showing that the large-distance decay rate is consistent with $r^{-4n}$.

This study focuses on solving the Stokes variational inequalities for ice sheet base sliding by employing a discrete mixed finite element approach based on Fenchel-Rockafellar duality. A continuous weak formulation of Stokes inequality is derived, along with proof of its well-posedness. An approximate solution is obtained by applying the finite element method, utilizing a discrete Fenchel-Rockafellar principle. Various discrete formulations are explored with different function spaces for pressure and the non-negativity constraint. Convergence results are established with detailed error estimates in specific norms for the velocity and pressure. Numerical experiments provide examples illustrating the method's applicability.

Using large-scale CO data, the authors calculated the outflow mass, energy, momentum, and kinetic power in two starbursting galaxies, LIRG galaxies PGC44020 and PGC42798. By comparing these values, the researchers found that both galaxies exhibit significant outflow kinetic power, accounting for a substantial fraction of their total starburst kinetic power. Observations also show that outflow mass rates correlate directly with star formation rates and starburst kinetic power in the galaxies. Furthermore, the analysis indicates that outflows in the galaxies primarily consist of gas rather than dust. Given the kinetic power, mass rates, and velocity of the outflows in the galaxies, they are likely to have a lasting impact on the galaxies' evolution. This is supported by evidence that the momentum in outflows is consistent with initial momentum from supernovae and momentum from radiative supernova explosions is more common in the galaxies.

Our research employed the event by event event-by-event analysis framework of the ANTONIO code, utilizing 2012 Pb-Pb collisions data from the ALICE experiment at the LHC. We examined the evolution of triangular flow $v_3$ in relation to centrality and transverse momentum, comparing our findings to experimental $v_3$ values and analyzing the event-by-event fluctuations of $v_3$ in terms of both transverse flow $\phi_3$ and angle $\psi_3$. We also investigated the correlations between elliptical and triangular flow parameters,蔓derived from x-y z plane positions and momentum directions of charged hadrons in various rapidity intervals. We discovered that the dependence of $\phi_3$ on centrality is significantly influenced by initial geometric eccentricity and correlations. Additionally, the dependence on centrality of the elliptical-flow to triangular-flow ratio $\rho_{23}$ indicates a decreasing trend with central collisions. We further noted a difference in behavior between $v_3$ measured in hadrons and in photons, with significant implications for understanding particle production and transport in the quark-gluon plasma.

Our proposed Flocking in Homogeneous Robots with Unknown Dynamics and Transparent Communication mechanism is designed for robotic swarm systems without relying on a common reference frame for communication. Although many robotic swarm systems employ crystal oscillators as a timekeeping mechanism, their timekeeping accuracy can vary between robots due to differences in internal components and software. To mitigate this, our FHUCTC mechanism utilizes a transparent algorithm to synchronize robot movements by scheduling communication based on the nearest future time according to each robot's local clock. During communication, incoming messages execute a tailored sequence of maneuvers specific to the message sender's dynamics, enabling swarm-wide flocking for robots with unknown dynamics.

Deep neural networks for semantic segmentation are typically pre-trained using image features extracted from natural videos. However, it's hypothesized that pre-training could also be highly effective without any manual labels, using depth information inferred from unlabeled videos instead of pre-defined depth datasets. A novel approach, called Self-Supervised Depth Pre-Training (SSDPT), is presented to automatically infer depth information from unlabeled videos and use it for self-supervised training of neural networks through a multi-task approach combining self-supervised depth estimation with CRF-posted CRF. A comprehensive evaluation of SSDPT across six video datasets shows that it consistently surpasses existing pre-training methods and competitive supervised approaches with significantly reduced model training and depth dataset usage.

Let's consider the set of all analytic functions defined within the unit disk in the complex plane and have their absolute value strictly less than one, denoted by the symbol. The classical Bohr inequality applies to any function expressed as a power series within the same domain, and it states the function's series expansion will still converge outside of the center of the disk by a certain margin of safety. The inequality states the function's series expansion will still converge at the boundary of the unit disk, but not exceed the center of the unit disk by more than the safety margin calculated as. The purpose of this essay is to elaborate on the proven Bohr inequality for analytic functions within the unit disk in the complex plane and have their absolute value strictly less than one, denoted by the symbol, as well as provide a historical overview of its inception, illustrating notable contributions to the field.

A nonparametric measure of correlation known as Kendall's tau is examined, along with an efficient method for estimating its value from data. The proposed method significantly reduces computational time by adapting a standard approach, allowing for quicker calculations when dealing with larger datasets. The modified approach specifically identifies key components in its underlying Hájek projection, leading to notable performance improvements while still providing accurate results with minimal additional CPU time compared to conventional methods.

The application of ITS technologies has led to substantial advancements in enhancing transportation efficiency, safety, and overall mobility. However, current ITS components are dependent on internet connections, restricting their effectiveness. A potential solution is to implement Edge Intelligence Systems to provide a more intelligent and efficient environment by enabling a flexible infrastructure that accommodates a diverse range of intelligent devices. This research focuses on addressing the security and privacy issues associated with EIS through clustering techniques. A security framework is being developed to protect data during the initial processing stage, as well as while transferring data to the processing nodes. Clustering is utilized to create a secure channel for data transmission to processing nodes and to verify the authenticity of processing nodes based on their security capabilities. Furthermore, this framework considers the privacy issues of the processing nodes and the intelligent devices to ensure a comprehensive approach to security.

This study focuses on the application of the Euler characteristic for advanced topological data analysis in multi-variable spaces. Euler characteristic is a fundamental, widely recognized topological invariant that has been extensively used in various fields, including physics and statistics. Advanced techniques for Euler characteristic have been developed for 2-dimensional univariate spaces and 3-dimensional volumes, and this research aims to extend their application to complex multi-variable spaces. We demonstrate the potential of EC in multi-variable spaces through a practical example, involving two-dimensional cell migration paths.

Our analysis focuses on an adjusted predator-prey model based on Holling-Tanner's equations, which incorporates a double-allee effect to account for scenarios where populations face a heightened risk of local extinction. This modified model is examined using phase plane and bifurcation analyses, with the goal of exploring conditions conducive to coexistence, to-and-fro dynamics, and potential extinction in the prey species. Notably, our investigation reveals bifurcation occurrences at critical densities andAL1 and AL2 points of ALLEE, with the findings of our study having the potential to inform the conservation and management of predator-prey ecosystems, especially when ALLEE point of ALLEE is present.

The Hirsch Conjecture has been proposed as a mathematical assertion stating that a d-dimensional polytope with n faces cannot have a diameter larger than n minus the maximum of two or the number of faces minus 1, but this is subject to the condition that d is at least the number of facets minus one. In 2010, Santos found a counterexample to this claim and demonstrated that it is invalid. In contrast, this text introduces an alternative, modified conjecture designed to prevent the occurrence of the disproof found by Santos. The revised conjecture is formulated as follows: let d be a dimension greater than 2, n be a number of facets, and P be a d-dimensional polytope; a sequence of faces indexed by i ranging from 0 to k is such that diameter is less than or equal to d for any hsc subgraph. The modified conjecture is then asked to be validated or disproven.

We explore in associative rings with unity how the symmetry of elements within a ring is connected with a modified version of Bass' nil-groups. Furthermore, we are investigating relationships between rank in these modified nil-groups and torsion, specifically $t > 0$, in rings that are also commutative in nature. It's shown that for every $t > 0$, there's a finite set of exceptions – rings $R_{t,1}, R_{t,2}, \dots$ – beyond which all $k$ in a specified range will have the same rank in $N_{*}(R)$ as in $N_{*}(R/\operatorname{rad} R)$, with these exceptions being the $t$-torsion rings $R_{t,i}$. The remaining $k$ in a specified range will then be incapable of factoring. As a result, this leads to the confirmed cases of the torsion conjecture, including its modified form.

This paper undertakes a thorough comparison of the comprehensive, off-shell computation for pp -> ttj events with the semistructured model commonly found in particle data tables, utilizing Fixed-Order Monte Carlo techniques. For this comparison to be fair, custom software called FASTERMC was created, capable of generating with Fixed-Order Monte Carlo events for specific processes such as ttj, W-lnu, Zll, single W and single t events. The analysis revealed significant off-shell and non-resonant influences on the distribution shapes of various observables, specifically top transverse momentum distributions, with notable implications for future analyses, including those related to Higgs production in association with top quarks, in analyses based on fixed-width histograms.

The susceptibility of facial recognition systems to deceptive attacks poses a significant challenge, particularly in deceptive use scenarios. Effective countermeasures against such threats rely on the accurate classification of deceptive images and videos, yet current approaches are hindered by the scarcity of available training data. To address this limitation, we propose an innovative method called DH-GAN that employs deep fake homeomorphic facial image generation. Utilizing a combination of convolutional neural networks and 3D superpixel representation, this method leverages both homeomorphic and non-homeomorphic image properties to efficiently capture data manifold structure. Consequently, this novel approach demands substantially less training data compared to existing techniques. Our experiments reveal that the generated homeomorphic images serve as an excellent representation of the homeomorphic concept and enhance the performance of facial detection systems. Implementing this technique in data augmentation results in improved classifications of homeomorphic images and diminished inaccuracies in deep fake detection, as evidenced by our empirical findings.

In the realm of autonomous vehicle control, supervised learning has been the prevailing approach, particularly when it comes to predictive modeling within autonomous driving systems. However, due to the inherent scarcity of labeled data, especially in the case of rare and critical situations, this approach, when applied under standard assumptions,, often,,,,,,,,,,,, fails to deliver the desired level of performance. To rectify this disparity, researchers have turned to more sophisticated methods that involve adapting their predictive models based on past experiences and lessons learned from them. By integrating these sophisticated methods with the existing predictive modeling techniques, researchers have successfully developed data-driven controllers that rely on past experiences and demonstrated their efficacy in the simulation of complex and challenging driving environments.

Evolutionary algorithms have seen significant advancements in recent years with the assistance of parallel processing techniques. However, varying evaluation times in search processes can negatively impact performance, creating a phenomenon known as evaluation time bias. To address this issue, a novel preemptive parallel evolutionary algorithm has been proposed, utilizing multiple cores to facilitate efficient processing. This new approach includes the development of two parallel strategies: one that ensures load-balancing and eliminates evaluation time bias, and another that promotes exploration. By integrating these strategies, parallel hybrid evolutionary algorithms have been developed, demonstrating improved performance over traditional methods, particularly in terms of search quality.

The recent microlensing event OGLE-2020-BLG-1844 presents a unique mass ratio system, situated at a critical point where the mass ratio between the star and planet shows significant sensitivity to the inner planet. By utilizing the maximum impact point and combining data from the IWA constraint, the derived planetary mass is found to be 2.07 times that of Jupiter. The event's long-duration anomaly and the absence of stellar caustic features suggest an inner planet with a low order number. The discovered system, with an estimated total mass of approximately 1.4 times that of the Sun, may correspond to an outer giant planet situated between an inner intermediate-mass planet and a brown dwarf. The system's characteristics include a semi-major axis of approximately 1.06 AU for the outer planet and approximately 0.16 AU for the inner brown dwarf, and it is estimated to be located at a distance of about 21.7 kiloparsecs. OGLE-2020-BLG-1844, with its high mass ratio and the presence of multiple planets, is a significant addition to the known OGLE-2011-BLG-117 and KMT-2019-BLG-179 systems.

The concept of an effective, time-independent Floquet generator emerged from analyzing periodically driven quantum systems, yet its characteristics remain unclear in many areas. Our research reveals that the effective Floquet generator actually exists in two distinct phases. One phase encompasses the conventional generator, while the second phase introduces a new, unique area, the weakly driving phase. Within this area, the generator's form relies on certain system properties such as bond-operator overlaps and phase factors associated with the evolution over one driving period. When moving outside the weakly driving phase, the Floquet generator develops non-perturbative corrections, which we've found can be expressed as non-Abelian random walks, providing new insights into generating quantum operations, particularly locality and magnetic fields, at various time scales.

Our research examined CePd$_{1-x}$Rh$_x$ samples where $0 \le x \le 1$ thoroughly using various techniques such as resistivity, X-ray diffraction, and magnetization measurements coupled with neutron inelastic scattering. Research revealed that nonmagnetic behavior dominates when $x$ exceeds approximately $x = 0.6$, while ferromagnetism appears at the edges of this range. Ferromagnetic ordering was found at temperatures of around $T_c = 2.05$ K ($x = 0.16$) and $T_c = 0.95$ K ($x = 0.84$). Within the magnetically ordered ferromagnetic phase of CePd$_{1-x}$Rh$_x$ ($x = 0.16$ and $0.84$), our neutron inelastic scattering data confirmed the emergence of spin-waves and spin-2 magnons.

The occurrence of HI narrow-line self-absorption features in the Central Molecular Zone has been investigated using a comprehensive study. A 43 cm HI survey, conducted with the Beijing yuemi Radio Telescope under the Beijing Haikou Summer School project, has been utilized to analyze the data. The survey, consisting of 37 star-forming regions and 3 empty fields, was conducted with high sensitivity and angular resolution. The results revealed multiple absorption features per spectrum, totaling 53 features detected. Furthermore, four regions exhibited a total of 21 features not initially detected. A significant number of features were detected in the central regions, specifically in 31 out of 37 regions. The resulting ZnrAZnrA value was found to be 0.92. The absorption features obtained were mostly characterized by narrow widths and moderate depths. The associated velocities, derived from the ZnrAZnrA value and the observed emission velocities, demonstrated a strong correlation with the systemic velocities of the investigated star-forming regions. The mean velocity of the absorption features was observed to be in agreement with the systemic velocity of the respective star-forming regions. The mean velocity of the absorption features was generally lower than the systemic velocity by approximately 0.5 km/s. The obtained absorption features were mostly characterized by narrow widths and moderate depths, indicating their occurrence in cold and dense molecular clouds. The implications of these findings are discussed in terms of the effects of star-forming regions and ultra-l

Research on uniform distribution of fractional parts of real numbers reveals a connection between intermediate beta-transformations and greedy beta-transformations incorporating a hole at zero. We establish this relationship in the context of an 'attractor set', which corresponds to the non-overlapping exchangeable shift space, specifically for $0<\beta<1/2$.

Determining the CP-violating phase phi_s resulting from mixing-induced phenomena in Bs decays is a crucial method for discovering potential new physics. Utilizing approximately 7,421 +/- 106 signal events from predominantly CP-odd final states (J/Psi phi), obtained via the decay of 7.84/fb data collected at the aforementioned energy by the LHCb detector, researchers performed an angular analysis on the decay modes of CP-odd components into J/Psi and phi particles. As a whole, this analysis yielded a precise determination of phi_s as approximately 0.017 +/- 0.062 (statistical) +/- 0.009 (systematic) radians, corresponding to roughly 3 degrees +/- 1 degree, and strongly aligning with the predictions rooted in the standard model. Furthermore, researchers conducted additional analyses aimed at detecting CP-violating phenomena occurring at various stages, including the production of CP-odd components, decay processes, and interactions with the environment. All observed results were found to be congruent with expectations according to the standard model.

It's widely acknowledged that deep neural networks excel at extracting meaningful features from data, but they generally struggle to apply these skills when features follow a different distribution. In this paper, a novel training technique is introduced that enables networks to adapt and perform well under varying distributional circumstances in unsupervised feature extraction. This adaptive training method leverages domain knowledge in the form of instance pseudo-labels derived from reliable, rule-based models and applies them to a large corpus from a different language. Experimental outcomes demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, and results further suggest that applying these pseudo-labels to a subset of the target corpus and refining it through the process of curating would yield even better outcomes when applied to a third dataset.

In finite fields of dimension 2, an arc is a subset of the 2-dimensional space such that no line intersects it at 3 or more points. The number of points in such an arc cannot exceed the larger of the field's characteristic or its square minus 1, with its parity determined by its dimension or its dimension minus 1, respectively. A construction of arcs meeting these bounds, first proposed by Odlyzkh in 1985, uses different fields at each point. Conversely, a recent study has found a complete example of an arc meeting these bounds, with all points sharing the same field but a specific nonconstant value assignment, applying to fields with a dimension of at least 5 and a characteristic of at least 5.
A visual demonstration reveals that there are $\binom{n+2}{5}$ equilateral triangles in a regular $n$-sided triangle grid.

Despite growing interest in explaining GNN predictions, existing methods are flawed: they fail to accurately represent GNN behavior, are highly sensitive to initial settings, and significantly slow down inference due to increased runtime. To overcome these issues, a new approach, LIME-GNN, is introduced. LIME-GNN addresses the suboptimal runtimes by utilizing GNN's efficient message passing and only running a local linear model outside of GNNs. Although practical, this method's results can be misleading due to the use of linear explanations. To improve scenario-based explanations, it incorporates a smoothing technique to mitigate noise in the environment, yielding faster and more reliable explanation generation. The proposed approach significantly improves explanation accuracy, reduces hyperparameter sensitivity, and achieves this in notably shorter runtime compared to leading methods.

The peculiar galaxy system RXCJ0232.2-4423, examined in this study, is a unique post-merger system that combines a radio galaxy with a cD galaxy. Its core, characterized by a bright region in X-rays, presents an atypical situation with low total mass but high radio mass. Researchers analyzed RXCJ0232.2-4423's X-ray data from Chandra and XMM-Newton to understand its radio galaxy's origin and discovered it is likely a radio galaxy within a cD galaxy due to a past merger. Its X-ray core is typical of cool cores and its gas distribution is relatively smooth outside a radio region, while showing a steep gradient in surface brightness. Furthermore, molecular gas is almost entirely consumed within a radio region, while molecular gas fraction decreases with distance. Researchers also found gas heated by radio galaxy's jets and accretion onto the cD galaxy. On a larger scale, gas rotates in a counter-clockwise manner, while radio system rotates clockwise. System's overall gas motion is complex, influenced by radio galaxy's jet activity and past merger's tidal forces, resulting in gas being pushed outwards and accumulating at system's periphery.

Recently, the Legendre Memory Unit (LMU), a novel type of recurrent neural network, has been introduced as a more efficient solution to the long-term dependencies issue often encountered in LSTM models, while also requiring fewer computational resources. In order to simplify the analysis process, an integrated implementation of LMU in the JAX framework was developed for time-series analysis and deep learning applications. Our study compares the performance characteristics of the Legendre Memory Function, its corresponding Legendre Memory Network and a over-parameterized variant, referred to as flat LMU, in terms of their ability to model long-term dependencies and their capacity for feature extraction. Furthermore, we explore the implications of applying LMU in various scenarios: as a standalone model and as a component within the architecture of a two-stage model. Our research also includes an examination of the effectiveness of LMU in different configurations when used in conjunction with a classifier and an encoder-decoder architecture.

Our focus lies in the area of particle physics research concerning particles that interact weakly with standard particles, which is the leading field for understanding dark matter, neutrino mass, and new fundamental forces. It's crucial to reevaluate the term "dark" in this context and explore the importance of lepton number even if it's not a fundamental quantity, revealing historical development, previous achievements, and ongoing experimental efforts, particularly in collider experiments.

Language evolution has been the subject of multiple research fields, with theoretical models being used to make predictions about the dynamics of language types within a population. We investigate the effect of a finite population's spatial arrangement and migration on language competition and the resulting complexity of the system. Our model considers the movement of individuals between nearby locations as the primary mechanism for migration, with the strength of this interaction being a key parameter. We discovered that migration can lead to the formation of monolingual areas separated by multilingual regions when the migration strength is above a critical threshold. We also found that limited migration promotes the emergence of multilingual areas at the expense of the potential for a single language to dominate the population. We further investigated the relationship between migration strength and the arrangement of languages within the population, observing a notable shift from a widely distributed language pattern at low migration strengths to a pattern of clustered language areas at high migration strengths. We analyzed the relationship between the arrangement of languages and the distribution of language types within the population, finding that a more ordered pattern corresponds to the existence of more diverse language types within the population.

The success of deep learning in solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with complex solutions has been well-documented. This paper delves into the convergence of neural networks when solving high-frequency PDEs with complex solution landscapes. We demonstrate that standard convergence criteria become inadequate in such scenarios and that wider networks are required to maintain convergence. By employing novel concentration and stability estimates for neural networks with high-frequency features, we derive bounds on the generalization error that depend on the inverse of the solution's frequency. These estimates confirm that wider networks are necessary to overcome this limitation. We validate our findings through experiments that support the existence of a fundamental trade-off between network width and the achievable error margin.

We examine a two-wave system in the interval (-1,1), where one wave undergoes Kelvin-Voigt damping while the other remains undamped. Our main findings show that under the condition of odd n, the energy decays at a rate of Sn for all observations on the undamped wave domain, provided the parameter a exceeds 1. Conversely, when n is even, the internal damping effect prevails, with the energy exhibiting faster decay at a rate of Sn+1 in A and Sb+1 in Σb. It's particularly noteworthy that our results confirm the critical Kelvin-Voigt damping behavior in this partial damping setup, in contrast to the rapid energy decay observed in the full domain Kelvin-Voigt damping case within the context of the wave equation framework.

Recent advances in deep reinforcement learning have led to widespread success across various applications, yet deep RL methods struggle with two key limitations: the need for extensive interactions and efficient handling of high-dimensional visual inputs. This paper introduces novel deep RL algorithms grounded in graph theory and Monte-Carlo tree search to overcome these challenges. It integrates value-based and action-based approaches to learn policies effectively, utilizing topological structures and environmental input graphs for its framework. This framework enables the learning of multiple, hierarchical objectives and the utilization of agent observations and input graph nodes. A new algorithm, Tree-search guided Monte-Carlo Value Learning (TMCVL), is proposed, utilizing Monte-Carlo value functions and policy evaluations through tree search. Experimental results demonstrate that TMCVL outperforms existing methods, including AlphaGo, in multiple tasks, including multiple games and multi-player games.

We've developed an all-optical method to produce non-reciprocal behavior in optical resonators without needing magnetic fields or unique materials. This technique exploits the generation of quantum squeezing in resonator modes, leading to sideband optical frequencies that interact through Kerr nonlinearity. This nonlinear interaction creates conditions for complete light blocking in one direction, but not the other, in T-shaped optomechanical resonators. We've demonstrated experimentally that this approach yields light blocking ratios of up to 10^6. Additionally, since a key component in our setup, the microtoroid resonator, is identical in all directions, a second instance can be incorporated without changing the light path, providing strong sources of non-reciprocal single photons.
